conf.description: F5 BIG-IP LTM system log (syslog-raw TMOS daemon messages), direct route: generic header + hex message-id parse, per-id dispatch for pool/node monitor status (01070638/01070639/01070640) rather than a global regex over free text, per recommendations.direct.cribl. Route-unrecognised message ids still get event.code/message populated. Keep _raw.

conf.comment: F5 BIG-IP LTM system log, syslog-raw, direct route. No Elastic integration covers OS-level syslog for this technology. The header/message-id/severity-digit extraction is generic per recommendations.direct.cribl; only the handful of pool/node monitor-status ids get a dedicated second-pass regex over the free-text message, everything else keeps event.code + message and nothing more. The RFC 3164 header carries no year or explicit timezone - auto_timestamp's own detection is used as a best-effort, not a verified conversion. pool_member's ip:port split uses a last-colon heuristic and will mis-split IPv6 members rendered with a space before the port (documented gap, not fixed).

functions.description: Pipeline purpose, message-id-lookup approach, and the timestamp/IPv6 gaps
Generic syslog header parse: timestamp, hostname, severity keyword, daemon[pid], hex message id, severity digit, free-text message
Pool member monitor/session status ids only: extract pool name, member, and status from the free-text message
Node monitor status id only: extract status from the free-text message (no pool context on a bare node event)
Copy service into log.syslog.appname and split pool_member address:port (last-colon heuristic, IPv6-space gap documented) - BEFORE rename
Batch rename of every mapped/custom (no-transform) field; message is already ECS's own field name so it is left as-is rather than renamed to itself
Set _time from the syslog header timestamp (no year/timezone in RFC 3164 - best-effort detection, not a verified conversion)
Tag event.dataset; drop now-consumed header scratch. _raw and message are deliberately kept.
